clue.text: Amusing lad edited miscellany

indicators.note: copy that has been edited is reworked, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A funny boy has put together a hotchpotch collection of writings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited' rearranges the ten letters of AMUSING LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmagundi is literally a mixed salad dish, and by extension any jumbled assortment or medley.

clue.text: Left artist exactly what's needed: a painting

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
RA is a Royal Academician, a stock crossword artist
'it' as in 'that's it', meaning just the thing required

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned by an artist finds a picture is all they want.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon is just a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is one kind of painting, a picture of a person, so this is definition by example.

clue.text: Swimmer's article seized by lawyers

indicators.note: something seized by another is held within it, so the article goes inside the lawyers

parts.note: the Bar is the collective body of barristers
'the' is the definite article

explanation.surface: A swimmer's piece of writing has been taken over by attorneys.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bathing in the sea or a pool is a swimmer, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Struggle with angle

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: Someone is wrestling with an awkward corner or a tricky perspective.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle on something is a point of view or perspective, a synonym.

clue.text: Straight new English bishop in vile collars

indicators.note: to collar is to grab round the neck, so the vile word encloses the rest

parts.note: ugly means vile, nasty
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
taken as written

explanation.surface: A frank, recently appointed English bishop is seized by horrible people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collars' puts NERRIN inside UGLY. 'Straight' is an adverb here, as in shooting straight.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot straight is to aim without missing, so the adverb means without error or deviation.

clue.text: Raving mad learner grabs one old instrument

indicators.note: a thing that grabs another holds it, so the one goes inside
mad suggests going wild, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

parts.note: L is the learner plate abbreviation
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wild, crazy pupil snatches up a single object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges RAVING to VIRGNA; add L, then 'grabs' puts I inside to make VIRG-I-NAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The virginal was a small keyboard instrument of the harpsichord family, popular in the 16th and 17th centuries.

clue.text: Scorer to do what setters do without

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the dogs' noise goes around the word to

parts.note: setters are gundogs, and dogs bark

explanation.surface: A musician is reluctant to do what puzzle setters do, a jibe from one setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setters' wants to be crossword compilers; here they are the gundogs. 'without' is used in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorer is someone who writes musical scores, and Béla Bartók was a Hungarian composer.

clue.text: Artist's intermittently good year

indicators.note: something done intermittently happens at intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A painter has had a patchy but generally successful twelve months.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was a celebrated Spanish painter and printmaker.

clue.text: Love a lecture Degas originally introduced

indicators.note: a thing introduced is brought in, so the initial goes into the other pieces

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech or lecture

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter of Degas is taken

explanation.surface: An art talk about Degas's work kindles the speaker's passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is intense love or worship, a synonym.

clue.text: Current chairman passes round golf flyer

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: the chairman goes round the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: Chairman Mao, the Chinese leader
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The present chair hands out something on golf to members.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final adult winged stage of an insect, so it is a flyer.

clue.text: Dull hack's book

parts.note: a matt surface is dull, not glossy
to hew is to hack or chop

explanation.surface: A tedious journalist has written a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' wants to be a writer; it is the verb to chop.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel of Matthew is the first book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Gunmen guard, say, a Times craft event

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so the gunmen go around the rest

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners
'say' introduces an example, eg
T is time, so TT is times

explanation.surface: Armed men protect a newspaper's handicraft fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a meeting for boat races, so an event for watercraft.

clue.text: Good sides keep fit in white

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the sides hold the fit letters

parts.note: L and R, left and right, are the two sides
A1 means in top condition; written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: Good teams stay in shape while dressed in white.
explanation.definitionFit: Glair is egg white used as a glaze or size, so it is a white.

clue.text: Bowler traps a Kent opener that appears in 12

indicators.note: the bowler traps the letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a spinner is a slow bowler in cricket

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so the first letter of Kent

explanation.surface: A spin bowler dismisses a Kent opening batsman at a big boat race.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinnaker is the large billowing sail racing yachts set downwind, so it is seen at boat races.

clue.text: Each boy wears black at the appropriate time

indicators.note: the boy is inside what he wears, so the black goes around him

parts.note: sable is black in heraldry
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Every lad dresses in black at the right moment, perhaps a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasonable means suited to the time of year or the occasion, timely.

clue.text: Food flown in for queen cooked jolly early

indicators.note: cooked as in cooked the books, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dinner flown in for the monarch was cooked cheerfully ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flown in' and 'queen' suggest royal catering; the queen is a bee and the flying is done by workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal jelly is the secretion worker bees bring to larvae destined to become queens.

clue.text: Citizen largely vandalised location of hangings

parts.note: a national is a citizen of a country

indicators.note: something vandalised is wrecked, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A citizen has done serious damage at a place of executions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hangings' suggests gallows; they are pictures hung on walls.
explanation.definitionFit: The London art museum on Trafalgar Square, where paintings are hung.

clue.text: Outside broadcast setting almost more offensive

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: scenery is a stage setting

explanation.surface: An outdoor broadcast's location is nearly more objectionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive or indecent; the comparative means more so.

clue.text: Paint bird and cat eating last of carcass

parts.note: the emu is a flightless Australian bird

indicators.note: the cat eats, taking the letter inside

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

indicators.note: the final letter of carcass is taken

explanation.surface: An instruction to paint a bird and a lion feeding on a dead body.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsion is a water-based household wall paint.

clue.text: Study coin displayed behind bars

indicators.note: the letters are laid out anew, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rare coin is exhibited in a locked case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind bars' fits the coin under protection, but means imprisoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held in custody means detained by police or jailed, an idiom for imprisonment.

clue.text: Carved 2s arrived with sailor

parts.note: came means arrived
OS is an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: Sculpted pictures turned up along with a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is PORTRAIT, so carved 2s are small sculpted portraits.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a carving, usually of a head in profile, in relief on stone or shell.

clue.text: Drunk one's out of it

parts.note: reads like someone too drunk to know what is going on, but means a cranium used as a drinking cup, as Norse warriors were said to do

explanation.surface: A drinker has passed out.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a vessel one has drunk from.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend has warriors drinking toasts from the bony heads of slain enemies, so this is a cup one drank from.

clue.text: Rocket placed on vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another is placed above it

parts.note: sat means placed, as in sat the baby down
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A firework has been stood on top of a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saturn V rocket launched the Apollo missions to the moon.

clue.text: A traveller gathered about 18

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative
met means gathered together

explanation.surface: A salesman assembled about a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is EMULSION, so the answer is another paint; 'about' reverses the whole string.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a paint made with egg yolk binding the pigment.

clue.text: Shade of paint in Tiepolo

indicators.note: of here means taken from within, so letters are drawn from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A colour found in the Venetian painter Tiepolo's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade of paint' wants to be the definition, but 'paint' holds the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint is a shade or variety of a colour.

clue.text: Couple hosts one extremely serious artist

indicators.note: a host holds guests inside, so the couple word goes round the rest

parts.note: to couple is to mate
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the extremes are the outside letters of serious

explanation.surface: A pair entertains one deeply earnest painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, leader of the Fauves.

clue.text: Make weepy film without one

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the one is removed

parts.note: a movie is a film
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Make a tear-jerker film without a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: To move someone is to stir their emotions, possibly to tears.

clue.text: Tearful woman's provincial honour

parts.note: Northern Ireland, NI, is known as the Province
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A woman cries at receiving an award from the regions.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is often called 'the Province' in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Niobe wept endlessly for her slain children and was turned into a weeping rock.

clue.text: Former PM's organ fund

parts.note: the liver is a bodily organ
a pool is a shared fund of money

explanation.surface: An ex-premier's body part is financed by a kitty.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Liverpool was British Prime Minister from 1812 to 1827.
